flagged.name: merge
flagged.visual: A single upward arrow whose shaft splits into two diverging branches at the top.
flagged.issue: Description depicts a fork/split (one input diverging into two outputs), which is the opposite of a merge. A merge icon should show two inputs converging into one output.

flagged.name: replace
flagged.visual: A small solid square at lower-left with a downward arrow above it and a dotted partial square at upper-right, suggesting drag-and-drop.
flagged.issue: Description depicts a drag-and-drop action, not a replace/find-and-replace operation. A replace icon should suggest swapping or substituting one thing with another.

flagged.name: vote
flagged.visual: A laptop with a checkmark displayed inside the open screen.
flagged.issue: A vote icon should resemble a ballot box, a voting form, or a hand depositing a ballot — not a laptop with a checkmark, which reads as 'task completed on device' or 'verified download'.

flagged.name: chart-gantt
flagged.visual: Three horizontal lines of decreasing length flush to a left axis line, with no bottom axis — a descending bar list.
flagged.issue: Description matches a simple sorted bar chart or filter icon, not a Gantt chart. A Gantt chart shows horizontal bars staggered at different vertical positions along a timeline, not flush-left bars of decreasing length.

flagged.name: table-cells-merge
flagged.visual: A rounded rectangle divided into three cells: one full-width top row and two equal cells in the bottom row.
flagged.issue: Description is essentially identical to table-cells-split. Both icons cannot share the same layout. A merge icon should depict cells being combined (e.g., two cells in the top row, one merged cell in the bottom row, or merge arrows), not a static layout identical to the split icon.

flagged.name: table-cells-split
flagged.visual: A rounded rectangle divided into two rows: the top row spans full width, the bottom row is split into two equal cells.
flagged.issue: Description is essentially identical to table-cells-merge. The two icons must differ visually. Either one of these descriptions is wrong, or both describe the wrong icon. A split icon should depict a cell being divided, which is distinct from a merged-cell layout.

flagged.name: newspaper
flagged.visual: Two overlapping document pages where the front page shows two horizontal text lines, representing a filled document being duplicated.
flagged.issue: A newspaper icon should resemble a folded newspaper with column-based text layout and a headline, not two overlapping document pages. The description sounds like a 'files' or 'copy' icon.

flagged.name: vault
flagged.visual: A rounded square containing a small circle at center with four short lines extending outward to each side, like a crosshair or hub.
flagged.issue: A vault icon should depict a safe or vault door — typically a large circular door with a combination wheel/handle and locking bolts. The description sounds like a network hub, crosshair, or settings icon, not a vault.

flagged.name: server-crash
flagged.visual: A rounded rectangle containing a lightning bolt with two small dots in opposite corners.
flagged.issue: A server-crash icon should show server units (stacked horizontal rectangles) with an error indicator such as a crack, X, or collision. The description matches a battery-charging icon, not a crashed server. The usage text in the data also misidentifies this as a battery icon.

flagged.name: bring-to-front
flagged.visual: Two rounded squares at opposite corners with bracket-like corner arcs connecting them, suggesting a swap or exchange.
flagged.issue: Bring-to-front should depict z-order elevation: a shape visibly layered on top of others (e.g., a solid shape overlapping a dimmed shape with an upward arrow). The description sounds like a swap or replace action, not a layer ordering operation.

flagged.name: send-to-back
flagged.visual: Two rounded squares of different sizes at opposite corners with small curved corner marks between them suggesting movement.
flagged.issue: Send-to-back should depict z-order demotion: a shape moved behind others (e.g., a shape behind others with a downward arrow). The description sounds like a move or reposition action, indistinguishable from bring-to-front, with no visual indication of layer direction.

flagged.name: wifi-high
flagged.visual: Partial Wi-Fi symbol — a dot at the bottom with two concentric arcs above it, indicating medium signal strength.
flagged.issue: The description explicitly says 'medium signal strength' and shows only two arcs. The icon name is wifi-high, which should show three arcs (strong/high signal). Two arcs would be medium/medium-high. The visual contradicts the 'high' designation.

flagged.name: file-archive
flagged.visual: A document page with a folded corner and a vertical ellipsis (three dots) on its face with a small circle below.
flagged.issue: A file-archive icon (compressed file, e.g. .zip) should show a zipper pattern, stacked layers, or a compression indicator on the document. A vertical ellipsis with a circle describes a 'more options' or version node overlay, not an archive file type.

flagged.name: banknote
flagged.visual: A landscape-oriented rounded rectangle with a small circle in the center flanked by two dots — resembling a credit or debit card.
flagged.issue: The description itself notes it resembles a credit card, not paper currency. A banknote icon should show a paper bill with printed detail (serial number lines, portrait oval, or decorative border), clearly distinguishable from the credit-card icon.

flagged.name: coins
flagged.visual: Two overlapping coin circles each showing a numeral, with a curved arrow between them suggesting a swap — depicting coin exchange or transfer.
flagged.issue: A coins icon should show a stack or pile of coins. The description depicts a currency exchange or transfer action with a swap arrow, which is a different concept. A plain coins icon should not include a directional arrow.

flagged.name: picture-in-picture
flagged.visual: A small rectangle in the lower-left corner of a larger rectangle, with an arrow pointing toward the smaller rectangle.
flagged.issue: The standard picture-in-picture icon places the small inset rectangle in the lower-right corner, not the lower-left. Left placement contradicts the canonical PiP convention and could be confused with a different layout variant.

flagged.name: separator-horizontal
flagged.visual: Two chevrons pointing up and down with a horizontal line between them, forming a sort or drag handle indicator.
flagged.issue: A separator-horizontal should depict a simple horizontal divider line (a rule or HR element). The description depicts a row-resize or sort-column handle, which is a functional control, not a static separator.

flagged.name: flip-horizontal
flagged.visual: Two square bracket characters flanking a vertical dashed center line, suggesting a resizable middle zone.
flagged.issue: A flip-horizontal icon should show a shape mirrored across a vertical axis (e.g., a triangle on the left reflected to produce a mirrored triangle on the right). The description of bracket characters flanking a dashed line suggests a column-resize handle, not a flip operation.

flagged.name: sticky-note
flagged.visual: A blank document page with a folded corner at the top right and noticeably rounded corners on all sides.
flagged.issue: A sticky note icon should resemble a small square memo note, typically with a folded corner at the top-left or bottom corner, often shown in a distinctive square aspect ratio. The description sounds nearly identical to the plain 'file' icon and does not distinguish a sticky note from a generic document.
